question: does 6x more training audio improve the student on prompts it has never seen?

arms.scaled_corpus_129: 129 curated utterances over 47 prompts (round 24), same objective and rate

autoencoder_ceiling.note: the scaled autoencoder's round-trip is indistinguishable from the recogniser's own noise floor on this split, so the *renderer* is not the limit any more

conclusion: 6x more training audio improves both proxies (DNSMOS 1.441 -> 1.537, mel cosine 0.9391 -> 0.9466) and the model stays two orders of magnitude faster than real time, but **WER on unseen prompts is ~1.0 in both arms**.  The round-23 headline (1.648 -> 0.667) was measured on the corpus's own texts, so it was partly fitting; with a prompt-disjoint hold-out the student is still at chance on new sentences.  That is the honest state, and it is exactly what a held-out split is for.
